label: prf:knot-eigenbasis-complete
title: Proof of Completeness of the knot-type eigenbasis
html:
Part (1). When q is not a root of unity, the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) is isomorphic to \mathbb{C}[S_n] as an abstract algebra (Jimbo's theorem), hence semisimple. By q-Schur--Weyl duality the image of H_n(R, q) in \mathrm{End}(V^{\otimes n}) is the commutant of \mathrm{SU}_q(2), which is the Temperley--Lieb quotient \mathrm{TL}_n(q); the decomposition of V^{\otimes n} is the standard result for \mathrm{SU}_q(2), see e.g. Chari--Pressley, Chapter 10. The restriction to partitions with at most two parts reflects \mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) = 1: the Young diagrams are at most two-rowed.

Part (2). Alexander's theorem guarantees surjectivity of the braid closure map \beta \mapsto \hat{\beta}. The Markov trace on H_n(R, q) is the unique trace satisfying the Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) for x \in H_n(R, q) and a parameter z determined by q (the \sigma_n^{-1} stabilisation then carries the derived loop value z_{-} = z - (q - q^{-1})). On each irreducible summand S_\lambda, the trace restricts to a non-zero scalar multiple of the character, so every summand is detected by some braid closure; the trivial braid already suffices, since \chi_\lambda(1) = \dim S_\lambda \neq 0.

Part (3). V_{\mathrm{phys}} := \varinjlim V^{\otimes n} is the algebraic direct limit along \iota_n(x) = x \otimes v_0 — the union of its finite-dimensional subspaces V^{\otimes n}, each of which is completely decomposed by (1) — and so the irreducible summands, indexed by the partitions \lambda with \ell(\lambda) \le 2, span V_{\mathrm{phys}}. The construction remains within rigid algebraic categories without any metric completion.
